traceability.notes:
The story docs/stories/007.0-DEV-ERROR-REPORTING.story.md defines improved, consistent, and actionable error reporting across all traceability rules, including specific messages, placeholders, suggestions, contextual data, and severity conventions.
Concrete evidence shows: - A dedicated Story-007 test suite (tests/rules/error-reporting.test.ts) validates the require-story-annotation rule’s error message, data payload (including functionName), and ESLint suggestions, directly covering REQ-ERROR-SPECIFIC, REQ-ERROR-SUGGESTION, REQ-ERROR-CONTEXT, and REQ-ERROR-LOCATION. - The other rules named in the story (require-req-annotation, require-branch-annotation, valid-annotation-format, valid-story-reference, valid-req-reference) each define clear, structured meta.messages aligned with the conventions (function, branch, format, and file/reference patterns), and are annotated in code with Story 007 requirements. - Tests for these rules (as seen in the Jest verbose run) exercise their error paths and, in the case of valid-story-reference and valid-annotation-format, explicitly verify detailed error-handling behavior, including filesystem errors and configuration errors. - The plugin’s configuration (src/index.ts) centralizes severities via TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES and exposes them through recommended and strict flat configs, with tests confirming that formatting issues are warnings and missing annotations/references are errors, exactly matching the severity conventions in the story.
Given the passing, story-tagged tests and the implemented messages, placeholders, suggestions, and severity mapping, all acceptance criteria and listed requirements for Story 007.0-DEV-ERROR-REPORTING are satisfied in the current codebase.
